title: Chemicals Hazard Rating System
description: The National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) hazard system for chemical materials. The NFPA 704 Diamond indicates health, flammability, reactivity and special hazards for common chemicals.

rows: 4 - SEVERE
Deadly, even the slightest exposure would be life threatening
Flash Point Below 73°F - Extremely flammable, volatile and explosive
May Detonate - May explode at normal temperatures and pressures
Radiation, Acid, Alkali, Corrosive, Oxidizer, Use No Water
3 - SERIOUS
Extreme Danger - Serious injury would result from exposure
Flash Point Below 100°F - Flammable, volatile or explosive at normal temperatures and pressure
Explosive - Capable of detonation or explosion by heat, shock or water
2 - MODERATE
Dangerous - Exposure would be hazardous to health
Flash Point Below 200°F - Moderately heated conditions may ignite
Unstable - Violent chemical changes possible at normal temperatures or when mixed with water
1 - SLIGHT
Irritation or minor injury would result from exposure
Flash Point Above 200°F - Substance must be preheated to ignite
Normally Stable - May become unstable at elevated temperatures or with water
0 - MINIMAL
No significant hazard or health risk
Will Not Burn
Stable - Remains stable with heat, pressure and water
